text:
sophia: Quick question — for enterprise tenants that want route-level routing policies surfaced in the Console's RBAC editor, what's the plan for quotas + telemetry? Need to show cost/latency per-route and allow scoping roles to routes. cc @jamal @devin

devin: We discussed this in infra sync but wasn't fully resolved. Two things: UI affordance for attaching quotas to route principals, and backend API to evaluate those at auth time. :thinking:

jamal: My take: keep the RBAC model minimal (resource + actions) and attach quota/telemetry as metadata objects, not permissions. Else the model explodes. Example: a role can allow invoke:on(routeX) and a separate quota object references that role+route.

elaine: That matches what security suggested. But product wants a one-click flow in the Console: "Give this role access to route X with monthly quota Y and telemetry ship-to dashboard Z". Need UX proposal.

devin: UX can be a builder that creates 2 API calls under the hood: one to Roles API, one to Quotas API. Example payloads: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/roles/{role_id}
{
  "allow": [
    {"resource": "route:payments:create", "actions": ["invoke"]}
  ]
}

POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/quotas
{
  "name": "payments-invoke-monthly",
  "scope": "role:role_id|resource:route:payments",
  "limit": "monthly:100000"
}
```

sophia: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) When evaluating a request at runtime, we need a cheap way to determine applicable quota without heavy DB joins. 2) Telemetry labels need to include role id + route id for attribution.

jamal: For runtime eval we can cache role->route bindings in authz cache (LRU) and precompute quota keys. AuthZ check returns a small header like `x-rw-quota-key: role_123|route_payments` and the quota service decrements.

elaine: That means the Console must show estimated delta for applying a quota (how it will affect monthly limits). Product asked for a preview panel: "If I assign this role 100k monthly, estimated cost = $X and p50 latency impact = +Y ms". We'll need telemetry-derived cost model.

devin: Telemetry team can provide a lightweight endpoint /models/cost-estimate that takes route_id + tokens_per_call + expected_qps and returns $/month + latency delta. We can wire that into Console as a preview.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: role-quota-service v1.3 deployed to staging at 2025-11-03T18:22:00Z :rocket:

jamal: Edge case: what about roles that span wildcard routes like `route:*`? Quota semantics become fuzzy. Suggest we allow "granularity" on quotas: exact, prefix, or wildcard. And the Console should warn when assigning quotas to wide-scoped roles.

sophia: Agreed. UX can show a red warning: "This quota will apply to N routes and may incur charges" and require a secondary confirmation.

elaine: Another constraint: Enterprise customers want audit trail showing who created the quota and when, plus a diff view for role changes. We need to include those in the rollout checklist.

devin: For the API, adding `created_by`, `created_ts`, and `change_id` is cheap. The Console will show a side-by-side diff using the change_id. Also add a telemetry tag `quota_change:{change_id}` to help correlate.

jamal: Implementation plan I propose:
1) Extend Roles API to accept a light `bindings` metadata array for UI-only annotations (non-enforced)
2) Quota service supports `scope` expressions e.g. `role:role_id|resource:route:payment*`
3) AuthZ cache publishes `role->route` resolution so runtime checks return quota keys
4) Console integrates cost-estimate model + confirmation flows + audit diff

sophia: Sounds solid. One API debate though: should quota lookup happen in the AuthZ path (synchronous) or as a separate preflight call to quota service? Latency sensitive.

devin: My vote: authz should return the quota key only. Actual decrement is async-ish but must be strongly consistent for strict quotas. For soft quotas we can be eventual. We'll need SLA tiers: Dedicated -> strict, Hosted -> soft by default.

elaine: Product likes that (tiered behavior). We'll document it in rollout docs and surface in Console with a label: "Enforcement: strict/soft".

jamal: Small implementation note: keep the cache invalidation strategy simple: TTL + event-based invalidation on role/route changes. Avoid expensive invalidation windows.

sophia: Okay next steps: Jamal/Devin prototype the authz cache changes + quota scope syntax. Elaine and Product will draft Console mockups with the preview/cost panel and confirmation flows. I'll collect telemetry needs and list of tags for integration.

devin: I'll open an RFC PR with the proposed API shapes and cache semantics.

jamal: I'll spike the cache patch in staging once RFC is up.

elaine: I'll put the mockups in Figma and share the link here when ready.

sophia: Thanks all. If we can get RFC + mockups this week we can aim for a canary next sprint. :+1:
